name: ADF4158CCPZ-RL7
title: ADF4158: 6.1 GHz fractional-N frequency synthesizer with direct modulation and waveform generation
summary: A fractional-N PLL synthesizer for RF inputs from 0.5 GHz to 6.1 GHz that closes a loop around an external VCO and loop filter. A fixed 25-bit modulus gives sub-hertz steps, and the part can sweep its output as sawtooth, triangular, parabolic or dual-rate ramps, with delays, FSK on the ramp and frequency readback, as well as FSK and PSK modulation; FMCW radar and communications test equipment are the named uses. It runs from 2.7 V to 3.3 V with a separate charge pump supply up to 5.5 V, is programmed over a 3-wire interface, and comes in a 24-lead LFCSP rated -40 °C to +125 °C.
key_figures: 5 mA high, 312.5 µA low, RSET = 5.1 kΩ
AVDD = DVDD = 2.7 V to 3.3 V; VP = AVDD to 5.5 V

operation.text: A fractional-N PLL synthesizer working with an external VCO and loop filter. The reference path is a ×2 doubler, a 5-bit R-counter and a ÷2 stage feeding the PFD; the feedback path is a prescaler and 12-bit INT counter steered by a third-order Σ-Δ fractional interpolator with a fixed 25-bit modulus, so N = INT + FRAC/2^25. A charge pump with RSET-programmed current drives CP. Lock detect, the counters and readback come out on MUXOUT. Eight 32-bit registers are written over a 3-wire serial port.
REFIN passes through switches and a buffer with a 100 kΩ bias resistor to the R-counter. In power-down the series switches open and a shunt switch closes, so the pin draws no load.
RFINA and RFINB are biased through 2 kΩ resistors from a 1.6 V bias generator, then a two-stage limiting amplifier makes the CML clock the prescaler needs.
The INT counter divides by 23 to 4095. The 5-bit R-counter divides REFIN by 1 to 32 to make the PFD reference.
The dual-modulus prescaler runs at CML levels on a synchronous 4/5 core. Set to 4/5 it handles up to 3 GHz, so above 3 GHz it must be 8/9. It sets the lowest INT: 23 with 4/5, 75 with 8/9.

The PFD compares the R and N counter outputs and drives the charge pump in proportion to their phase and frequency difference. A fixed delay sets an antibacklash pulse of about 3 ns, which removes the dead zone and keeps the reference spur level steady.

Data clocks into a 32-bit shift register MSB first on each CLK rising edge; LE rising moves it to one of eight latches chosen by control bits C3, C2, C1 (DB2:0). The digital section holds a 5-bit R-counter, 12-bit N-counter and 25-bit FRAC counter.

The LSB fraction, R-counter, reference doubler, charge pump current and RDIV2 are double-buffered: a new value written to its register takes effect only on the next write to R0. To change the fraction, write R1 then R0; the frequency moves after the R0 write.

Bits M4 to M1 in R0 select what MUXOUT shows: three-state, DVDD, DGND, R or N divider output (direct or halved), digital lock detect, serial data, the CLK divider output, the fast-lock switch state, or readback.
Read timing is specified into a 10 pF load with 100 µA IOL and 100 µA IOH current loads referred to 1.5 V. LE is held high through readback.

Setting CSR enable shortens lock time. It needs a 50 % duty cycle at the PFD (RDIV2 gives this), the charge pump current at its minimum setting, and positive phase detector polarity; it does not work with negative polarity.

RDIV2 puts a divide-by-2 flip-flop between the R-counter and PFD, giving a 50 % duty cycle. With the doubler off the REFIN falling edge is the active PFD edge; with it on both edges are active. The highest REFIN allowed with the doubler on is 30 MHz.
CPI4 to CPI1 in R2 set the current in sixteen steps from 0.31 mA to 5 mA (with RSET = 5.1 kΩ); program the current the loop filter was designed for.
INT normally loads before FRAC, so for about four PFD cycles the N value can be wrong and, if INT changed, the loop can overshoot. Setting DB15 of R3 delays the INT load so both change together.
With R3 DB14 at 0 (the usual setting) the modulator resets on every R0 write; set it to 1 to avoid that.
Digital lock detect sets after 24 consecutive PFD cycles of 15 ns (LDP = 0) or 40 (LDP = 1).
R3 DB6 = 1 for a VCO with positive tuning characteristic, 0 for negative.

CE low, or R3 DB5 = 1, powers down. Register contents are kept until supplies are removed. In power-down dc current paths are removed, counters go to their load state, the charge pump three-states, lock detect resets, RFIN is debiased, and the input register still accepts and latches data. R3 DB4 three-states the charge pump alone; R3 DB3 holds the RF counters in reset.
R4 DB31 = 1 synchronizes LE to the reference internally.

Writing 01110 to R4 DB[30:26] turns the Σ-Δ modulator off, making channel spacing equal to fPFD and removing the fPFD/2^26 offset. Both fraction fields must be 0, and after R4 is written R3 is written twice (DB3 = 1, then DB3 = 0) to reset the counters. Ramping, PSK, FSK and phase adjust are then unavailable. Normal operation uses 00000.

R4 DB[24:23] = 11 turns on a constant negative bleed current that keeps the charge pump clear of its dead zone, keeping phase noise and spurs low; it matters most for channels near multiples of the PFD frequency. Bleed current and readback to MUXOUT cannot be used together.

Readback to MUXOUT (R4 DB[22:21]) gives the synthesizer frequency at the moment of an interrupt. A rising edge on TXDATA triggers the interrupt, which reads the ramp's INT and FRAC; R5 DB[27:26] chooses whether the sweep then continues or stops at that frequency.

The 12-bit CLK1 divider in R2 sets the duration of each time step in a ramp. The 12-bit CLK2 divider in R4 is the CLK2 timer for ramp mode and also sets how long the loop stays wide in fast-lock mode; R4 DB[20:19] pick ramp divider or fast-lock divider, 00 when neither is used.

R3 DB[11:10] choose continuous sawtooth, continuous triangular, single sawtooth or single ramp burst; R0 DB31 turns the ramp on. Each step's size is set by the signed 16-bit deviation word and the 4-bit deviation offset (which sets the deviation resolution) in R5; the number of steps by the 20-bit step word in R6. A second deviation word and step word allow a second ramp (ramp 2 enable), and R5 also enables the parabolic ramp, the FSK ramp, and clocking the ramp from TXDATA instead of the clock divider.
R7 enables a delayed start, a delay between ramps and a fast-lock during ramp delay. The 12-bit delay start word sets the delay, counted in PFD clocks or in PFD × CLK1 clocks (DB16).
FSK and PSK are enabled in R3 and keyed from TXDATA. FSK can be superimposed on a ramp.
Reserved bits are written 0.
The exposed paddle connects to GND. AVDD, DVDD and SDVDD run at one voltage; VP may be higher, up to 5.5 V.
